label: Find things in the inbox, draft replies, never send
authored_by: the site, as a starting point — not measured, not surveyed; the first thing to argue with
description: We connected Gmail to Claude so it could find things in the inbox, answer questions about it, and draft replies for a person to send themselves. Reading is what was wanted. Nobody asked it to send mail as them — Google's own consent screen already permits it, and only the per-action approval prompt stands between the two.

notes.send.message.world: refused; bounded today only by the approval prompt, which is a setting and not a boundary — an org owner can remove it
notes.read.message.tenant: wanted — and reads every message the account can already read, which is more than most people picture when they say "read my mail"
notes.create.schedule.tenant: refused; a filter is a rule that keeps acting on mail after the chat ends, and nobody asked for one
